subject: Request: extended nightly finalization window for RetailMax bulk inference
messages:
From: Jane Carter <jane.carter@retailmax.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@retailmax.com
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly bulk finalization - request for extended window

Hi Vivek,

Quick note from our ops team: last night the nightly_bulk_v2 job had a very long tail — roughly 11% of jobs stayed in RUNNING past our 6hr expectation and were marked FAILED by our orchestrator, which triggered reruns and duplicate downstream writes. We attached the run logs (nightly-run-logs-20271025.zip) for your reference.

Can Redwood provide an SLA carveout so we can extend the job completion window for this workload from 6 hours to 12 hours while we (RetailMax) investigate root cause and harden retries on our side? Important constraints from our end: we can provide an idempotency token per job and maintain original payloads for 72 hours — but we need confirmation on how Redwood will handle safe retries, dedupe, and any compensating controls.

Also: if this extension is approved, will Redwood accept temporary deviation from the standard latency SLO without triggering automatic breach credits, or would you prefer to formalize via a short contract amendment? We want to minimize customer impact while keeping compliance teams in the loop.

Thanks — can you loop in engineering and legal as needed?

—Jane
Jane Carter
Head of ML Ops, RetailMax

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jane Carter <jane.carter@retailmax.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly bulk finalization - request for extended window

Jane — thanks for the detail and the logs. We reviewed the traces and agree the long-tail is borderline for the current 6hr finalization window. Id like to propose a short-term, controlled exception and a technical guardrail package so you can avoid failed completions and duplicate downstream effects.

Proposal (summary):
- Scope: nightly_bulk_v2 job class (all RetailMax accounts for that job).
- Duration: 3 months (trial period) starting as soon as both sides sign the amendment.
- Completion window: extended from 6 hours -> 12 hours for FINALIZED decision state.
- Retry policy: Redwood will enable automated safe retries for runs that time out between 6-12 hours. Retries are gated by a valid idempotency-key and checksum match.
- Idempotency requirements (client side): provide an idempotency-key per logical job (X-Idempotency-Key), keep original input payload and checksum accessible for 72 hours.
- Server-side enforcement (Redwood):
  - Reject retry attempts without a matching idempotency-key or with mismatched checksum.
  - Dedup store TTL: 72 hours; dedupe resolution window: 48 hours recommended for downstream consumers.
  - Max retry attempts: 3 (exponential backoff with jitter).
- Credits and SLAs: we can offer a temporary operational credit mechanism rather than automatic breach: if more than 2 finalization incidents per month for this workload occur due to platform behavior, Redwood issues a 5% monthly service credit for that month.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Engineering (Ben) to confirm the implementation details and monitoring hooks.
2) Legal/AM (Laura) to prepare a short amendment and DocuSign for the 3-month exception.
3) RetailMax to confirm you can (a) attach idempotency-key and (b) retain payload/checksums for 72h.

Ill attach a short template SLA-exception form and a technical idempotency checklist. If everyone agrees, we can aim to flip this on within ~5 business days.

Regards,
Vivek
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly bulk finalization - request for extended window

Looping in the infra details — thanks for the ask, Vivek. Below are the concrete server-side controls we can enable immediately to satisfy the proposal. These will be part of the technical annex we push to the amendment.

Implementation notes (actionable):
- Idempotency header: accept X-Idempotency-Key (UTF-8, max 128 chars) at job submit time and persist atomically with the job record.
- Checksum: we validate a client-supplied sha256(payload) at finalize time. Retries must include the same checksum header (X-Payload-SHA256) or be rejected with 409 Conflict.
- Dedup store: Redis cluster (dedupe:jobs) with TTL=72h; we recommend 48h dedupe window for downstream to avoid late duplicates.
- Retry state machine: signal retries only for jobs in state RUNNING that hit the 6hr soft cutoff; retried jobs will be identical replays (same job idempotency key).
- Max retries: 3 with exponential backoff (base 60s) and randomized jitter +/-20%.
- Finalization lock: finalize step takes a distributed lease (10s) and double-checks checksum before committing outputs — this ensures at-most-once finalization semantics for a given checksum+idempotency-key pair.
- Monitoring & alerts: create a RetailMax-specific dashboard and two alert tiers: (1) >1.5% long-tail rate in 24h (warning) and (2) >3% (pager).

Attachments: idempotency-api-spec.md, dlq-playbook.pdf (technical annex).

We can flag a feature toggle in Dedicated and Hosted control planes named "extended_finalization_window:RetailMax:nightly_bulk_v2". If RetailMax wants Dedicated-only behavior we can scope it, otherwise it will be a tenant-level flag.

If this looks reasonable Ill schedule a 30-minute handoff with RetailMax ops to walk the checklist.

—Ben
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
